A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, Retaining by Doing: The Role of On-Policy Data in Mitigating Forgetting. All 18 pages of each version, including figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A.1–A.5, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original Llama/Qwen post-training experiments, Gaussian-mixture simulations, ablations, and appendix analyses of forgetting.

after.justification: v2 retains the original model experiments, simulations, ablations, and appendix analyses, including the results in Figures 2–9 and Tables 1–2.

M1.justification: The SFT, Self-SFT, GRPO, REINFORCE, Iterative-SFT, and SFT-on-RL-data procedures are unchanged. Revised descriptions of prior methods in Section 5 do not alter the evaluated procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions use IFEval, MMLU, and Countdown as target tasks, with MATH, WildJailbreak, and WildGuardTest as additional non-target evaluations. The Gaussian simulation scenarios are also unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout: SFT/Self-SFT/GRPO comparisons, REINFORCE in Table 1, Iterative-SFT in Figure 7, and SFT trained on RL data in Figure 9.

E3.justification: Sections 2–4 and Appendices A.1–A.5 retain the same models, splits, sample sizes, metrics, learning rates, training budgets, and testing procedures. No new evaluation protocol is introduced.

E4.justification: The learning-rate/epoch tests, KL-regularization and advantage-estimator comparisons, Gaussian-distance sensitivity tests, RL-trace SFT experiment, and KL–forgetting analysis retain the same questions and evidence.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The statistical estimation and reporting in Appendix A.5 are unchanged.

E6.justification: The numerical entries in Tables 1–2 and plotted results in Figures 2–9 are unchanged. Appendix A.5 retains the Pearson correlation of 0.52 and the same non-monotonic KL–forgetting finding.

T1.justification: The forward/reverse KL identities, Gaussian-mixture definitions, overlap-based quantities, and total-variation derivation in Section 3 and Appendix A.2 remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the claims that RL forgets less than SFT, on-policy data explains this robustness, and approximately on-policy data can mitigate forgetting.

C2.justification: The mechanism explanations, applicability qualifications, and stated limitations are unchanged. Appendix A.5 replaces its closing criticism of Shenfeld et al. with 'still not fully understood,' restating the existing caution about the KL–forgetting relationship.

D1.justification: Appendices A.1 and A.3 retain identical simulation settings, training hyperparameters, data splits, prompts, and software/hardware information. The code-availability statement and repository link are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 5 adds Razin et al. (2024; 2025) on reward variance and RL optimization speed. It also tempers the characterization of SFT memorization and describes RAFT/STaR as approximately on-policy RL; Appendix A.5 softens its positioning against Shenfeld et al.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized prose and grammar edits in Sections 4.2–5 and Appendix A.5, updates the version stamp, and adds Cisco Research to the funding acknowledgment. Section order and overall narrative structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 1's caption is rewritten to emphasize that GRPO's advantage estimator does not explain its robustness to forgetting. Its table structure and all figure graphics remain unchanged; the bibliography undergoes limited spacing and pagination changes.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves precision and readability. Section 5 replaces 'SFT mostly memorizes' with 'can be prone to memorization,' clarifies the approximately on-policy characterization of RAFT/STaR, and adds optimization context. Table 1's revised caption states the comparison's purpose more clearly. These are limited gains; the empirical evidence, mathematical content, reproducibility information, and substantive limitations remain unchanged.
